Sí, ese commit fue casi todo de seguridad. Lo de root lo hablamos el 19 de octubre y decidimos dejarlo como está, a propósito y documentado. No llegamos a cambiarlo.

Tener acceso al socket de Docker equivale a ser root en el host. Usar un usuario SSH que no sea root pero esté en el grupo `docker` da el mismo poder, así que tampoco lo resuelve.
- **Lo que decidimos fue limitar quién tiene cuenta.** Por eso pasamos a cuentas personales con 2FA opcional y una página de Actividad que registra qué hace cada cuenta. Registra todo salvo lo que se escribe dentro de las consolas. Está explicado en `README.md:209`, el punto "Every account is root on your servers".

#!/bin/sh -e

# Signs a published release so instances with Update automatically install it
# (see app/services/self_update.rb). Run it on your own machine after the
# Release workflow has pushed the image. The private key never goes to GitHub:
# that's what keeps someone who takes over the account or the registry from
# shipping code to every instance.
#
# Once, before the first signed release:
#   cosign generate-key-pair --output-key-prefix ~/.config/kamal-web/release-signing
#   cp ~/.config/kamal-web/release-signing.pub config/release-signing.pub   # and commit it
#
# Then, for each release:
#   bin/sign-release v1.2.0

tag=${1:?usage: bin/sign-release vX.Y.Z}
key=${KAMAL_WEB_SIGNING_KEY:-$HOME/.config/kamal-web/release-signing.key}
repository=$(ruby -e 'load "config/initializers/version.rb"; print KamalWeb::REPOSITORY')
image="ghcr.io/$repository"

cmp -s "${key%.key}.pub" config/release-signing.pub || { echo "${key%.key}.pub doesn't match config/release-signing.pub" >&2; exit 1; }

digest=$(docker buildx imagetools inspect "$image:$tag" --format '{{json .Manifest.Digest}}' | tr -d '"')
echo "Signing $image:$tag ($digest)"
echo "Check it matches the digest in the Release workflow's summary before you go on."
cosign sign --key "$key" --annotations "tag=$tag" "$image@$digest"
cosign verify --key config/release-signing.pub --annotations "tag=$tag" "$image:$tag" >/dev/null
echo "Signed. Instances pick it up within the hour."

class Project < ApplicationRecord
  include RefreshesStatusBoard
  SOURCE_KINDS = %w[ git local discovered ].freeze
  # Commands that only start, stop or reroute existing containers, so they are
  # safe on a discovered project whose config was rebuilt without env or secrets.
  DISCOVERED_MUTATIONS = %w[ app_start app_stop app_maintenance app_live accessory_start accessory_stop accessory_restart ].freeze
  NOTIFICATION_FORMATS = %w[ generic slack discord ].freeze

  has_many :environment_variables, -> { order(:destination, :key) }, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :project_files, -> { order(:path) }, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :command_runs, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :console_sessions, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :server_metrics, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :hourly_metrics, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :health_checks, dependent: :delete_all
  has_many :alerts, dependent: :delete_all

  has_secure_token :deploy_webhook_token, length: 36
  # Proves a deploy webhook call comes from CI or the git host, on top of the
  # URL's token. See DeployHooksController.
  has_secure_token :deploy_webhook_secret, length: 36, on: :create

  encrypts :ssh_private_key, :git_ssh_private_key, :git_access_token, :notification_webhook_url, :discovered_files, :deploy_webhook_secret

  normalizes :repository_url, :local_path, :branch, :config_file, with: ->(value) { value.strip.presence }

  validates :name, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :source_kind, inclusion: { in: SOURCE_KINDS }
  validates :notification_format, inclusion: { in: NOTIFICATION_FORMATS }
  validates :branch, :config_file, presence: true
  validates :repository_url, presence: true, if: :git?
  validates :repository_url, format: { with: %r{\A(https://|ssh://|[\w.-]+@[\w.-]+:)\S+\z}, message: :invalid_git_url }, allow_blank: true
  validates :local_path, presence: true, if: :local?
  validates :discovered_service, presence: true, if: :discovered?
  validates :notification_webhook_url, format: { with: %r{\Ahttps?://\S+\z} }, allow_blank: true
  validate :config_file_is_relative
  validate :local_path_inside_projects_root, if: :local?
  validate :ssh_keys_are_private_keys

  scope :ordered, -> { order(:name) }

  after_save :register_servers, if: :saved_change_to_config_snapshots?
  after_destroy_commit :remove_clone
  after_destroy_commit :ignore_discovered_service, if: :discovered?

  def git?
    source_kind == "git"
  end

  def local?
    source_kind == "local"
  end

  def discovered?
    source_kind == "discovered"
  end

  def discovered_file_map
    JSON.parse(discovered_files.presence || "{}")
  end

  def allows_command?(command)
    !discovered? || !command.mutating? || command.key.in?(DISCOVERED_MUTATIONS)
  end

  def source_description
    if git? then "#{repository_url} · #{branch}"
    elsif local? then local_path
    else I18n.t("projects.form.kind_discovered")
    end
  end

  def workspace_path
    if local?
      Pathname.new(local_path)
    else
      Rails.configuration.x.workspaces_path.join("project-#{id}")
    end
  end

  # Destination names as found in the last config sync. The base config
  # (no -d flag) is represented by nil.
  def destinations
    config_snapshots.keys.sort.map(&:presence).presence || [ nil ]
  end

  def config_for(destination)
    KamalConfigSnapshot.new(config_snapshots[destination.to_s])
  end

  def hosts
    config_snapshots.values.flat_map { |snapshot| KamalConfigSnapshot.new(snapshot).all_hosts }.uniq
  end

  def register_servers
    Server.register(hosts)
  end

  # A host can serve several destinations, e.g. staging and production on
  # the same machine.
  def destinations_for_host(host)
    destinations.select { |destination| config_for(destination).all_hosts.include?(host) }
  end

  def destination_for_host(host)
    destinations_for_host(host).first
  end

  # Variables for the base config apply everywhere; destination-specific ones
  # override them.
  def environment_for(destination)
    variables = environment_variables.to_a
    base = variables.select { |variable| variable.destination.nil? }
    scoped = variables.select { |variable| destination.present? && variable.destination == destination }
    variables = (base + scoped).to_h { |variable| [ variable.key, variable.value.to_s ] }

    # A discovered project has no git checkout to take the version from.
    version = discovered? && discovered_versions[destination.to_s]
    version ? variables.reverse_merge("VERSION" => version) : variables
  end

  # Projects without their own key use the instance key from Settings.
  def ssh_keys
    [ ssh_private_key.presence || Setting.instance.ssh_private_key, git_ssh_private_key ].compact_blank
  end

  # Latest monitoring sample per host, which tells whether SSH works.
  def latest_metrics
    hosts.filter_map { |host| server_metrics.where(host: host).order(collected_at: :desc).first }
  end

  # Mutating commands on a protected destination need its name typed to run
  # from the browser. The base config is stored as "".
  def protected_destination?(destination)
    protected_destinations.include?(destination.to_s)
  end

  # Form checkboxes send "." for the base config, since "" is what an empty
  # selection sends.
  def protected_destinations=(names)
    super(Array(names).compact_blank.map { |name| name == "." ? "" : name.to_s }.uniq)
  end

  def confirmation_word(destination)
    destination.presence || name
  end

  def active_operation
    command_runs.active.find(&:mutating?)
  end

  def last_deploy(destination = :any)
    runs = command_runs.where(kind: %w[ deploy redeploy rollback setup ]).where.not(status: %w[ queued running ])
    runs = runs.where(destination: destination) unless destination == :any
    runs.order(created_at: :desc).first
  end

  LiveRelease = Data.define(:version, :created_at)

  # The version running for a destination, from the containers in the latest
  # monitoring samples, so apps deployed outside Kamal Web show up too.
  def live_release(destination, metrics = latest_metrics)
    config = config_for(destination)
    prefix = [ config.service, config.primary_role, destination.presence ].compact.join("-") + "-"
    container = metrics.reject(&:error).flat_map(&:containers).select do |container|
      labels = container["Labels"] || {}
      container["State"] == "running" && labels["service"] == config.service && labels["role"] == config.primary_role &&
        labels["destination"].to_s == destination.to_s && container["Names"].to_s.start_with?(prefix)
    end.max_by { |container| container["CreatedAt"].to_s }

    if container
      LiveRelease.new(version: container["Names"].delete_prefix(prefix), created_at: (Time.zone.parse(container["CreatedAt"].to_s) rescue nil))
    elsif discovered? && (version = discovered_versions[destination.to_s])
      LiveRelease.new(version: version, created_at: nil)
    end
  end

  private
    # Only clones made by Kamal Web are removed; mounted folders are left alone.
    def ignore_discovered_service
      Setting.instance.ignore_service!(discovered_service)
    end

    def remove_clone
      root = Rails.configuration.x.workspaces_path.expand_path
      FileUtils.rm_rf(root.join("project-#{id}")) unless local?
    end

    def config_file_is_relative
      if config_file.present? && (config_file.start_with?("/") || config_file.split("/").include?(".."))
        errors.add(:config_file, :not_relative)
      end
    end

    def local_path_inside_projects_root
      return if local_path.blank?

      root = Rails.configuration.x.projects_path.expand_path.to_s
      path = File.expand_path(local_path)
      unless path == root || path.start_with?("#{root}/")
        errors.add(:local_path, :outside_root, root: root)
      end
    end

    def ssh_keys_are_private_keys
      { ssh_private_key: ssh_private_key, git_ssh_private_key: git_ssh_private_key }.each do |attribute, key|
        next if key.blank?
        errors.add(attribute, :not_private_key) unless key.include?("PRIVATE KEY-----")
      end
    end
end

# registered automatically on every sync; others can be added by hand before

content.text: Antes de construirlo necesito cerrar unas decisiones que cambian bastante el diseño:

questions.question: ¿Qué debe poder hacer Kamal Web con las bases de datos en tus servidores?

options.label: Crear y registrar (Recomendado)
options.description: Como Hatchbox: Kamal Web levanta el contenedor del motor (por SSH, en la red 'kamal', con volumen y contraseña generada) y también permite registrar uno que ya exista.

options.label: Solo registrar existentes
options.description: Tú levantas el servidor de BD (accessory de Kamal, instalado a mano...) y Kamal Web solo guarda la conexión y crea bases/usuarios dentro.

questions.question: ¿Qué motores soportamos en la primera versión?
Al attachear una BD a una app, ¿qué hace Kamal Web?

options.label: Crea BD + usuario y fija la variable (Recomendado)
options.description: Crea una base y un usuario propios para la app (en managed: usa la URL que pegues), guarda DATABASE_URL como variable cifrada del proyecto/destino y te ofrece redeploy. La app debe tener DATABASE_URL en env.secret; el check del overview avisará si falta.

options.label: Solo fija la variable
options.description: Guarda la URL de conexión como variable del proyecto, sin crear bases ni usuarios.

questions.question: Si la BD está en otra máquina distinta a la de la app, ¿cómo llega la app a ella?

options.label: Puerto publicado con IPs permitidas (Recomendado)
options.description: El contenedor publica el puerto y Kamal Web sólo lo abre a las IPs de los servidores de las apps attacheadas (regla de firewall con iptables DOCKER-USER). Con TLS en Postgres/MySQL.

options.label: Red privada
options.description: Asumes una red privada (VPC de DigitalOcean, Tailscale...) y Kamal Web publica el puerto sólo en la IP privada que indiques.

options.label: Solo misma máquina
options.description: Las BDs creadas por Kamal Web sólo se attachean a apps en el mismo servidor; las remotas se tratan como 'managed' (URL).

# A backup of everything that can't be recreated: the main database (projects,
# encrypted secrets, history) and the secret_key_base that decrypts it. Clones,
# caches and queues are left out.
#
# Restoring stages the archive as storage/restore.tar.gz; script/apply_restore.rb
# swaps the files in when the container next boots, before the database opens.
module InstanceBackup
  # The message is a key under flash.backups.invalid.
  class Invalid < StandardError; end

  APP = "kamal-web".freeze
  ENTRIES = %w[ manifest.json database.sqlite3 secret_key_base ].freeze
  MAX_SIZE = 500.megabytes
  STAGED_PATH = Rails.root.join("storage", "restore.tar.gz")
  # Scheduled backups, when turned on in Settings.
  DIRECTORY = Rails.root.join("storage", "backups")
  STORED_NAME = /\Akamal-web-backup-\d{8}-\d{6}\.tar\.gz\z/

  module_function

  def filename
    "kamal-web-backup-#{Time.current.strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")}.tar.gz"
  end

  def write(io)
    Dir.mktmpdir("kamal-web-backup") do |dir|
      database = File.join(dir, "database.sqlite3")
      # VACUUM INTO writes a consistent copy while the app keeps running.
      ActiveRecord::Base.connection.execute("VACUUM INTO #{ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(database)}")
      manifest = { app: APP, version: KamalWeb::VERSION, created_at: Time.current.iso8601 }.to_json

      gzip = Zlib::GzipWriter.new(io)
      Gem::Package::TarWriter.new(gzip) do |tar|
        add(tar, "manifest.json", manifest)
        add(tar, "database.sqlite3", File.binread(database))
        add(tar, "secret_key_base", Rails.application.secret_key_base)
      end
      gzip.finish
    end
    io
  end

  # Writes a backup into the volume and deletes the oldest beyond keep.
  def store!(keep:)
    FileUtils.mkdir_p(DIRECTORY, mode: 0o700)
    path = DIRECTORY.join(filename)
    partial = DIRECTORY.join(".#{path.basename}.partial")
    File.open(partial, "wb", 0o600) { |file| write(file) }
    File.rename(partial, path)
    stored.drop(keep).each(&:delete)
    path
  end

  # Newest first.
  def stored
    return [] unless DIRECTORY.directory?

# A PostgreSQL or Redis server that apps can be attached to. Kamal Web either
# runs it in a container on one of the servers ("created"), uses a container
# that is already there ("existing", such as a Kamal accessory) or only knows
# its URL ("external", such as a DigitalOcean managed database).
class Database < ApplicationRecord
  ENGINES = %w[ postgresql redis ].freeze
  SOURCES = %w[ created existing external ].freeze
  IMAGES = {
    "postgresql" => %w[ postgres:18 postgres:17 postgres:16 ],
    "redis" => %w[ valkey/valkey:8 redis:7 ]
  }.freeze
  PORTS = { "postgresql" => 5432, "redis" => 6379 }.freeze
  VARIABLES = { "postgresql" => "DATABASE_URL", "redis" => "REDIS_URL" }.freeze
  URL_SCHEMES = { "postgresql" => %w[ postgres postgresql ], "redis" => %w[ redis rediss ] }.freeze

  belongs_to :server, optional: true
  has_many :attachments, class_name: "DatabaseAttachment", dependent: :restrict_with_error

  encrypts :password, :url

  normalizes :name, :container_name, :admin_user, :url, with: ->(value) { value.strip.presence }

  validates :name, presence: true, uniqueness: { case_sensitive: false }, format: { with: /\A[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*\z/ }, length: { maximum: 40 }
  validates :engine, inclusion: { in: ENGINES }
  validates :source, inclusion: { in: SOURCES }
  validates :server, presence: true, unless: :external?
  validates :container_name, presence: true, format: { with: /\A[\w.-]+\z/ }, unless: :external?
  validates :container_name, uniqueness: { scope: :server_id }, allow_nil: true
  validates :image, inclusion: { in: ->(database) { IMAGES.fetch(database.engine, []) } }, if: :created?
  validates :admin_user, format: { with: /\A\w+\z/ }, allow_nil: true
  validates :public_port, numericality: { only_integer: true, in: 1024..65_535 }, allow_nil: true
  validates :url, presence: true, if: :external?
  validate :url_matches_engine, if: -> { external? && url.present? }

  before_validation :set_defaults, on: :create

  after_update_commit :refresh_attachments, if: -> { saved_change_to_public_port? || saved_change_to_url? || saved_change_to_password? }
  broadcasts_refreshes

  scope :ordered, -> { order(:name) }

  ENGINES.each { |name| define_method(:"#{name}?") { engine == name } }
  SOURCES.each { |name| define_method(:"#{name}?") { source == name } }

  def default_variable
    VARIABLES.fetch(engine)
  end

  def internal_port
    PORTS.fetch(engine)
  end

  def volume_name
    container_name if created?
  end

  # Where the server keeps the files the container mounts.
  def files_directory
    "$HOME/.kamal-web/databases/#{container_name}"
  end

  # A created container serves PostgreSQL over TLS with its own certificate,
  # so apps on other servers connect with sslmode=require.
  def tls?
    created? && postgresql?
  end

  # Redis servers have one shared password; PostgreSQL gets a user per app.
  def shared_password
    password if redis?
  end

  def address_for(app_hosts)
    if external?
      nil
    elsif app_hosts.all? { |host| host == server.host }
      [ container_name, internal_port ]
    elsif public_port
      [ server.host, public_port ]
    end
  end

  def manager
    DatabaseManager.new(self)
  end

  # Runs the container. Called from ProvisionDatabaseJob, since pulling the
  # image can take a while.
  def provision!
    update!(status: "provisioning", status_message: nil)
    manager.provision
    update!(status: "running", status_message: nil, checked_at: Time.current)
    manager.apply_firewall if public_port
  rescue RemoteShell::Error, DatabaseManager::Error => error
    update!(status: "failed", status_message: error.message, checked_at: Time.current)
  end

  def check!
    status = manager.status
    manager.apply_firewall if created? && public_port && status == "running"
    update!(status: status, status_message: nil, checked_at: Time.current)
  rescue RemoteShell::Error, DatabaseManager::Error => error
    update!(status: "failed", status_message: error.message, checked_at: Time.current)
  end

  # Hosts of apps on other servers, which the firewall lets in.
  def remote_app_hosts
    attachments.includes(:project).flat_map(&:app_hosts).uniq - [ server&.host ]
  end

  def remove!(delete_data: false)
    manager.remove(delete_data: delete_data) if created?
    destroy!
  end

  private
    def set_defaults
      self.container_name ||= "kamal-web-db-#{name}" if created?
      self.admin_user ||= "postgres" if postgresql? && !external?
      self.password ||= SecureRandom.hex(24) if created?
      self.status = "external" if external?
    end

    def url_matches_engine
      scheme = URI.parse(url).scheme
      errors.add(:url, :wrong_scheme, schemes: URL_SCHEMES.fetch(engine, []).join(", ")) unless scheme.in?(URL_SCHEMES.fetch(engine, []))
    rescue URI::InvalidURIError
      errors.add(:url, :invalid)
    end

    def refresh_attachments
      attachments.each(&:write_variable!)
    end
end

  normalizes :variable, with: ->(value) { value.strip.upcase.presence }

  validates :variable, presence: true, format: { with: /\A[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*\z/, message: :invalid_name }
  validates :variable, uniqueness: { scope: [ :project_id, :destination ] }
  validates :database_name, uniqueness: { scope: :database_id }, allow_nil: true
  validate :destination_configured
  validate :variable_free, on: :create
  validate :reachable, on: :create
  validate :redis_database_free, on: :create

  before_validation :set_credentials, on: :create

  # Creates what the app needs on the database server and stores the URL.
  def attach!
    transaction do
      save!
      database.manager.create_user(self) if database.postgresql? && !database.external?
      write_variable!
    end
    database.manager.apply_firewall if database.created? && database.public_port
    true
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid
    false
  end

  # With delete_data the app's database and user are dropped. Otherwise they
  # stay, but the user can no longer sign in.
  def detach!(delete_data: false)
    transaction do
      environment_variable&.destroy!
      destroy!
      database.manager.remove_user(self, delete_data: delete_data) if database.postgresql? && !database.external?
    end
    database.manager.apply_firewall if database.created? && database.public_port
  end

  def write_variable!
    variable_record = environment_variable || project.environment_variables.new(key: variable, destination: destination)
    variable_record.update!(value: url)
    update_column(:environment_variable_id, variable_record.id) unless environment_variable_id == variable_record.id
  end

  # The hosts the app's containers run on.
  def app_hosts
    destinations = destination ? [ destination ] : project.destinations
    destinations.flat_map { |name| project.config_for(name).roles.values.flatten }.uniq
  end

  def remote?
    database.address_for(app_hosts)&.first == database.server&.host
  end

  def url
    return database.url if database.external?

    host, port = database.address_for(app_hosts)
    if database.postgresql?
      query = "?sslmode=require" if database.tls? && remote?
      "postgres://#{username}:#{password}@#{host}:#{port}/#{database_name}#{query}"
    else
      credentials = ":#{CGI.escape(database.shared_password)}@" if database.shared_password.present?
      "redis://#{credentials}#{host}:#{port}/#{redis_index}"
    end
  end

  # Kamal only passes variables listed under env.secret to the app.
  def listed_in_config?
    destinations = destination ? [ destination ] : project.destinations
    destinations.all? do |name|
      raw = project.config_for(name).raw_config || {}
      envs = [ raw["env"], *raw.fetch("servers", {}).then { |servers| servers.is_a?(Hash) ? servers.values : [] }.map { |role| role["env"] if role.is_a?(Hash) } ]
      envs.compact.any? { |env| env.is_a?(Hash) && Array(env["secret"]).any? { |name| name.to_s.split(":").first == variable } }
    end
  end

  private
    def set_credentials
      return unless database

      if database.postgresql? && !database.external?
        self.database_name ||= [ project&.name, destination, (variable unless variable == "DATABASE_URL") ].compact.join("_").downcase.gsub(/[^a-z0-9]+/, "_").gsub(/\A_+|_+\z/, "").first(63)
        self.username ||= database_name
        self.password ||= SecureRandom.hex(24)
      elsif database.redis? && !database.external?
        used = database.attachments.pluck(:redis_index)
        self.redis_index ||= (0...REDIS_DATABASES).find { |index| !used.include?(index) }
      end
    end

    def destination_configured
      errors.add(:destination, :unknown) if destination && project && !project.destinations.include?(destination)
    end

    def variable_free
      return unless project && variable

      if project.environment_variables.exists?(key: variable, destination: destination)
        errors.add(:variable, :taken_by_variable)
      end
    end

    def reachable
      return if database.nil? || project.nil? || database.external?

      errors.add(:base, :not_reachable, port: database.internal_port) unless database.address_for(app_hosts)
      errors.add(:base, :not_running) unless database.status == "running"
    end

    def redis_database_free
      errors.add(:base, :no_redis_database) if database&.redis? && !database.external? && redis_index.nil?
    end
end

require "shellwords"

# Runs a database's container on its server and manages what lives in it,
# over SSH with the server's access. Docker and iptables run through sudo
# when the SSH user isn't root.
class DatabaseManager
  class Error < StandardError; end

  PRELUDE = <<~SH.freeze
    set -e
    if [ "$(id -u)" = 0 ]; then S=; else S="sudo -n"; fi
    if docker info >/dev/null 2>&1; then D=docker; else D="$S docker"; fi
  SH

  CERTIFICATE_PATH = "/etc/kamal-web".freeze
  # The uid both the postgres and redis/valkey images run as.
  IMAGE_UID = 999

  def initialize(database)
    @database = database
  end

  def provision
    run(<<~SH)
      dir="#{@database.files_directory}"
      mkdir -p "$dir" && chmod 700 "$dir"
      umask 077
      #{write_files}
      $S chown #{IMAGE_UID}:#{IMAGE_UID} #{mounted_files.keys.map { |name| %("$dir/#{name}") }.join(" ")}
      $D network create kamal >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      $D pull -q #{q @database.image} >/dev/null
      $D rm -f #{q container} >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      $D run --detach --name #{q container} --network kamal --restart unless-stopped \\
        --label kamal-web.database=#{q @database.name} --log-opt max-size=10m \\
        --volume #{q @database.volume_name}:#{data_path} \\
        #{mounted_files.keys.map { |name| %(--volume "$dir/#{name}:#{CERTIFICATE_PATH}/#{name}:ro") }.join(" ")} \\
        #{"--publish 0.0.0.0:#{@database.public_port}:#{@database.internal_port}" if @database.public_port} \\
        #{q @database.image} #{command} >/dev/null
      for i in $(seq 60); do
        if #{ready_check}; then exit 0; fi
        sleep 1
      done
      $D logs --tail 20 #{q container} 2>&1
      echo "The database didn't start within a minute."
      exit 1
    SH
  end

  # running, stopped or missing for containers; reachable or unreachable for
  # external databases, from a TCP connection.
  def status
    return external_status if @database.external?

    output = run(<<~SH).strip
      state=$($D inspect -f '{{.State.Status}}' #{q container} 2>/dev/null) || { echo missing; exit 0; }
      if [ "$state" = running ] && #{ready_check}; then echo running; else echo "${state:-stopped}" | sed 's/^exited$/stopped/'; fi
    SH
    output.lines.last.to_s.strip.then { |state| state == "running" || state == "missing" ? state : "stopped" }
  end

  def create_user(attachment)
    psql(<<~SQL)
      DO $$BEGIN
        IF EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = '#{attachment.username}') THEN
          ALTER ROLE "#{attachment.username}" WITH LOGIN PASSWORD '#{attachment.password}';
        ELSE
          CREATE ROLE "#{attachment.username}" WITH LOGIN PASSWORD '#{attachment.password}';
        END IF;
      END$$;
      SELECT 'CREATE DATABASE "#{attachment.database_name}" OWNER "#{attachment.username}"' WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_database WHERE datname = '#{attachment.database_name}')\\gexec
    SQL
  end

  def remove_user(attachment, delete_data: false)
    if delete_data
      psql(<<~SQL)
        DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS "#{attachment.database_name}" WITH (FORCE);
        DROP ROLE IF EXISTS "#{attachment.username}";
      SQL
    else
      psql(<<~SQL)
        DO $$BEGIN
          IF EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = '#{attachment.username}') THEN
            ALTER ROLE "#{attachment.username}" WITH NOLOGIN;
          END IF;
        END$$;
        SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE usename = '#{attachment.username}';
      SQL
    end
  end

  # Only the hosts of attached apps on other servers (and containers on the
  # kamal network) reach the published port. Docker's DOCKER-USER chain sees
  # the packets before they are forwarded to the container. The rules don't
  # survive a reboot, so CheckDatabasesJob applies them again.
  def apply_firewall
    accepted = @database.remote_app_hosts.map { |host| "$S iptables -A #{chain} -s #{q host} -j RETURN" }
    run(<<~SH)
      $S iptables -N #{chain} 2>/dev/null || $S iptables -F #{chain}
      subnet=$($D network inspect kamal -f '{{range .IPAM.Config}}{{.Subnet}} {{end}}' 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}')
      [ -n "$subnet" ] && $S iptables -A #{chain} -s "$subnet" -j RETURN
      #{accepted.join("\n")}
      $S iptables -A #{chain} -j DROP
      #{firewall_rule("-C")} 2>/dev/null || #{firewall_rule("-I")}
    SH
  end

  def remove(delete_data: false)
    run(<<~SH)
      $D rm -f #{q container} >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      #{"$D volume rm #{q @database.volume_name} >/dev/null 2>&1 || true" if delete_data}
      rm -rf "#{@database.files_directory}"
      while #{firewall_rule("-D")} 2>/dev/null; do :; done
      $S iptables -F #{chain} 2>/dev/null || true
      $S iptables -X #{chain} 2>/dev/null || true
    SH
  end

  private
    def run(script, input: nil)
      shell = RemoteShell.for_server(@database.server)
      if input
        shell.run(PRELUDE + script, input: input, check: true)
      else
        shell.run(PRELUDE + script, check: true)
      end
    end

    def psql(sql)
      command = "$D exec -i #{q container} psql -X -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U #{q @database.admin_user} -d postgres"
      run(command, input: sql)
    end

    def external_status
      uri = URI.parse(@database.url)
      Socket.tcp(uri.host, uri.port || @database.internal_port, connect_timeout: 5).close
      "reachable"
    rescue SystemCallError, SocketError, IOError, URI::InvalidURIError
      "unreachable"
    end

    def container
      @database.container_name
    end

    def chain
      "KAMAL-WEB-DB-#{@database.id}"
    end

    def firewall_rule(action)
      "$S iptables #{action} DOCKER-USER -p tcp -m conntrack --ctorigdstport #{@database.public_port.to_i} --ctdir ORIGINAL -j #{chain}"
    end

    def q(value)
      Shellwords.escape(value.to_s)
    end

    def data_path
      if @database.postgresql?
        # PostgreSQL 18 images keep their data one level up, by major version.
        @database.image.split(":").last.to_i >= 18 ? "/var/lib/postgresql" : "/var/lib/postgresql/data"
      else
        "/data"
      end
    end

    # Written to the server with umask 077, from base64 so the content never
    # needs quoting.
    def mounted_files
      @mounted_files ||=
        if @database.postgresql?
          key, certificate = self.class.certificate(@database.container_name)
          { "postgres.env" => "POSTGRES_PASSWORD=REDACTED, "server.key" => key, "server.crt" => certificate }
        else
          { "redis.conf" => "requirepass #{@database.password}\nappendonly yes\n" }
        end
    end

    def write_files
      mounted_files.map { |name, content| %(echo #{Base64.strict_encode64(content)} | base64 -d > "$dir/#{name}") }.join("\n")
    end

    def command
      if @database.postgresql?
        "-c ssl=on -c ssl_cert_file=#{CERTIFICATE_PATH}/server.crt -c ssl_key_file=#{CERTIFICATE_PATH}/server.key"
      else
        "#{server_binary} #{CERTIFICATE_PATH}/redis.conf"
      end
    end

    def server_binary
      @database.image.start_with?("valkey") ? "valkey-server" : "redis-server"
    end

    def ready_check
      if @database.postgresql?
        "$D exec #{q container} pg_isready -q -h 127.0.0.1 -U #{q @database.admin_user} >/dev/null 2>&1"
      else
        cli = @database.image.to_s.start_with?("valkey") ? "valkey-cli" : "redis-cli"
        "$D exec -e REDISCLI_AUTH #{q container} #{cli} ping 2>/dev/null | grep -q PONG"
      end
    end

    class << self
      # A self-signed certificate: apps use sslmode=require, which encrypts
      # without verifying it.
      def certificate(name)
        key = OpenSSL::PKey::EC.generate("prime256v1")
        certificate = OpenSSL::X509::Certificate.new
        certificate.version = 2
        certificate.serial = SecureRandom.random_number(2**64)
        certificate.subject = certificate.issuer = OpenSSL::X509::Name.parse("/CN=#{name}")
        certificate.public_key = key
        certificate.not_before = Time.current
        certificate.not_after = 10.years.from_now
        certificate.sign(key, OpenSSL::Digest::SHA256.new)
        [ key.to_pem, certificate.to_pem ]
      end
    end
end

      redirect_to @database, notice: t("flash.saved", name: @database.name)

  end

El panel **Bases de datos** ya funciona en local: está en la barra lateral entre "Servidores" y "Usuarios". Todavía no está commiteado ni desplegado. Lo he probado con contenedores reales de Postgres y Valkey en tu Docker, pero aún no contra un VPS de verdad.

**Tipos de base de datos que se pueden añadir:**
- **Creada por Kamal Web:** levanta Postgres (16/17/18) o Valkey/Redis en un contenedor del servidor que elijas, en la red `kamal`, con un volumen para los datos y una contraseña generada. Postgres va con TLS.
- **Contenedor existente:** registras uno que ya esté corriendo, por ejemplo un accessory de Kamal, y Kamal Web crea bases y usuarios dentro.
- **Externa o managed:** pegas la URL (por ejemplo una de DigitalOcean) y se le pasa a la app tal cual.

**Conectar una app** se hace desde la página de la base de datos:
- En Postgres cada app tiene su propia base y su propio usuario, y el usuario de una app no puede conectarse a la base de otra.
- En Redis cada app tiene su propio número de base.
- La URL se guarda como variable cifrada del proyecto (`DATABASE_URL` o `REDIS_URL`), para todos los destinos o solo para uno.
- Si el `deploy.yml` de la app no tiene esa variable en `env.secret`, la página te avisa y te dice qué línea añadir. Después hay que hacer redeploy.

**Si la app está en otro servidor:**
- Hay que indicar un "puerto para otros servidores". Solo pueden entrar las IPs de los servidores de las apps conectadas, con reglas de iptables que se vuelven a aplicar cada 5 minutos porque se pierden al reiniciar.
- Esto necesita root o `sudo` sin contraseña en el servidor de la base de datos.

**Desconectar y borrar:**
- Al desconectar una app se borra su variable y su usuario ya no puede entrar, pero los datos se quedan, salvo que elijas borrarlos.
- Al eliminar una base de datos creada por Kamal Web puedes conservar el volumen.

En la prueba real comprobé que se conecta por la red `kamal`, que la conexión remota va con TLS, que una IP no permitida no entra y que la autenticación de Valkey funciona con un cliente Ruby. La prueba encontró dos fallos que los tests no detectaban, ya corregidos:
- Postgres no recibía la contraseña.
- Por defecto, cualquier usuario podía conectarse a la base de otra app.

Los 239 tests pasan, y rubocop y brakeman no dan avisos. Lo he documentado en el README y lo he traducido a los 8 idiomas. Los contenedores, el volumen y la red de la prueba ya están borrados de tu Docker.

¿Lo commiteo, pusheo y despliego?
